newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish food group Avonmore says set for growth.
newsitem.headline: Irish food group Avonmore says set for growth.

text.p: Irish food group Avonmore Foods on Monday reported higher profits and said it was well positioned for further growth in 1997, particularly in the British dairy and meat sector and the U.S. cheese and food ingredients business.

"We are well resourced and we are confident of further growth," group secretary Brendan Graham told Reuters after the group reported a 13.7 percent rise in 1996/7 pre-tax profits to 36.45 million Irish pounds ($57.5 million).
He said the group's worldwide milk pool increased by five percent to almost 500 million gallons during 1996 and the group was well set to top that in 1997.

Avonmore said its operations in Ireland, the United Kingdom and the U.S. were firmly established and adapting well to changing circumstances. The group was confident of continuing profit and earnings growth in the current year.
It said it was particularly pleased with its growth potential in the United States and Britain.

"Growth opportunities in the U.K. dairy and meat sectors and in the U.S. cheese and food ingredients market are being followed up," Avonmore said, noting that turnover from the group's U.S. operations increased by 27 percent to 218 million Irish pounds during 1996.
"Avonmore West is a very strong performer and very well positioned in the U.S.," Graham said.

He said the U.S. division had consolidated its position as the largest north-west U.S. cheese and whey-based food ingredients manufacturer and the group's presence will be further boosted by a $20 million capital investment plan, to be completed by mid-1997.
Avonmore expects its U.S. operations to produce 100,000 tonnes of the group's total cheese output of 145,000 tonnes in 1997.

Avonmore Dairies, the fifth largest liquid milk supplier in England and Wales, increased its share of the British liquid milk market primarily through the growth of sales to retail multiples, the group said.
Graham predicts further sales and margin growth as milk costs reduce. This should underpin continuing margin improvement, he said.

In Ireland the company's milk products division was affected from early in the year by a fall in world dairy product prices but maintained buoyancy by "switching operations to higher margin products".
Further sales growth for meat products is expected in Irish and European markets in 1997, it added.
